title: Astrid and the Veil
premise: Astrid Vane, a memory-thief turned reluctant bookkeeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the guild's ledgers record debts owed by the crown itself: centuries ago, King Aldric bargained his name to a creature called the Veil, which has worn him like a puppet ever since. When a feral child named Sef arrives speaking the dead tongue of the first kingdoms, Astrid realizes the girl is a living ledger — the last unspent page of Aldric's bargain. To free the king, Astrid must steal back what she once sold to survive her own past, even as the Veil hunts Sef and the guild's masters reveal they intend to renew the bargain rather than end it. In the dragon-fire vault beneath the capital, Astrid burns her stolen memories as payment to unbind Aldric, choosing truth over the comfortable lies of loyalty; the Veil unravels, Sef remembers who she is, and Astrid walks out with an empty mind but a full heart, beginning again.
about_author: Emrys Oyelaran is a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about debts, names, and the people brave enough to remember out loud.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Astrid balances the guild's impossible accounts by day and steals memories from desperate clients by night, keeping one vial of her own sold childhood hidden in her sleeve. A routine entry — 'one king's shadow, overdue' — makes her blood run cold. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competent routine.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. A mud-caked child appears at the guild door speaking a language older than any kingdom, and every ledger in the building opens itself when she speaks. The guildmaster orders the child locked away; Astrid, unsettled by recognition in the girl's eyes, disobeys. Emotional beat: protective instinct overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Thief Isandro Whitlock, hired to burgle the palace, witnesses King Aldric speak in two voices at once — his own and something vast behind it. He escapes with a scrap of royal memory showing Aldric signing away his name. Emotional beat: horror curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Price She Already Paid
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Interrogating Sef through drawings and fragments, Astrid realizes the child carries the original contract of Aldric's bargain — and that Astrid's own sold memories were the down payment, taken from her family generations ago. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro brings his stolen fragment to the guild to sell, colliding with Astrid, who recognizes the handwriting as her own ancestor's. The guildmasters convene secretly and vote to renew the bargain rather than break it. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forged in mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Hunt Through Hollow Streets
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. The Veil, wearing the king's body, comes for Sef; Astrid and Isandro flee through the city's forgotten underways while Sef's speech grows stronger, unraveling enchantments as she goes. Emotional beat: breathless flight deepening into trust.

chapters.title: Ledger of Betrayals
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Cornered, Isandro trades Sef's location to the guildmasters to save his own skin — then, hearing the Veil's true voice through the walls, realizes he has fed a child to it. He turns on his buyers. Emotional beat: shame transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Dragon-Fire Vault
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Beneath the capital lies the last living dragon-fire, the forge where the first bargain was struck. Sef recites the contract whole; the Veil arrives wearing the king, and Astrid learns the only currency it accepts is freely surrendered memory. Emotional beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Astrid. Astrid feeds her stolen childhood — and every memory of Isandro and Sef — into the fire, paying the debt in full. Aldric tears free of the Veil, which unravels screaming into ash; Sef speaks her own name for the first time. Emotional beat: sacrifice as triumph.

chapters.title: Beginning Again
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Memoryless but alive, Astrid relearns the world as Isandro and Sef refuse to let her face it alone; the guild falls, its ledgers burned or freed. In the final scene, Astrid writes a new first line in a blank book: her own name. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal.
